case_title: AK Devaiah v. State of Karnataka
accused_caste: Kodava community (as stated by the accused in his statement; the court made no separate finding)
victim_caste: Kodava community (per defence submission, not a court finding)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498-A; IPC s.304-B; Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 ss.3, 4, 6
weapon: None mentioned (the victim poured kerosene on herself and set herself on fire)
evidence_type: Medical (post-mortem), testimonial (sister, brother and brother-in-law of the victim), recovery of ornaments, inquest statements
confession: None (the accused denied the incriminating circumstances and admitted only reporting the death to police)
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged and accepted dowry demand with mental and physical cruelty; death within about eleven months of marriage; the appellant allegedly habitually consumed liquor; the appellant allegedly pledged the victim's ornaments
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of all charges under ss.498-A and 304-B IPC and ss.3, 4, 6 Dowry Prohibition Act
high_court_outcome: State's appeal allowed; acquittal set aside; convicted under ss.498-A and 304-B IPC and ss.3, 4, 6 Dowry Prohibition Act; 7 years for s.304-B; 5 years and Rs 15,000 fine for s.3
offence_finally_established: Dowry death under IPC s.304-B; cruelty under IPC s.498-A; offences under Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3, 4 and 6
neutral_facts: The victim was married to the accused in April 1989 and lived in the accused's house in Bangalore. The victim worked for a private company in addition to household duties. Before the marriage, the accused allegedly demanded dowry in the form of cash of Rs 15,000 and gold and silver ornaments. Part of the cash and most of the ornaments were allegedly handed over before the marriage, with further cash given at the time of the marriage, and the balance promised after marriage. The prosecution alleged that after the marriage the accused, who allegedly drank alcohol, subjected the victim to mental and physical cruelty, including over the balance of the dowry. Quarrels also arose from the absence of pregnancy after marriage. On 16 March 1990, about eleven months after the marriage, the victim set herself on fire with kerosene in the house at about 5:00 AM. The accused informed the police station about the unnatural death at about 7:10 AM. The police registered a case, and a magistrate conducted an inquest, recording statements of the victim's blood relatives. A case was then registered on the basis of those materials. The post-mortem examination found 97% ante-mortem burns, a smell of kerosene, and death due to shock from burns; no symptoms of pregnancy were found. The accused was arrested on 18 March 1990. Following information given during interrogation, the accused went with the investigating officer and witnesses to a pawnbroker's shop, where pledged ornaments of the victim were recovered. The victim's sister, brother and brother-in-law testified that the accused demanded and accepted dowry and subjected the victim to mental and physical cruelty.
offence_severity: Minimum 7 years; maximum imprisonment for life (IPC s.304-B(2) as quoted in the judgment)
physical_harm: Death of the victim from 97% ante-mortem burns (second and third degree burns over most of the body) and resulting shock
financial_property_loss: Dowry cash of Rs 15,000 and gold and silver ornaments (all except a pair of gold bangles) allegedly given to the accused
motive: Demand for the balance of dowry and cruelty over that demand, as accepted by the court on the basis of the witness evidence
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent testimony of PWs 1-3 (sister, brother and brother-in-law of the victim) on dowry demand and cruelty; post-mortem findings; recovery of ornaments
witness_credibility: Court found PWs 1-3 consistent; the High Court's reliance on their evidence was upheld; trial court's acquittal held wholly perverse
post_offence_conduct: Accused reported the death to police; ornaments were pledged by the accused and later recovered from a pawnbroker (prosecution case, not separately commented on by the court)
trial_duration: offence: 16-3-1990; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 25-8-2005; Supreme Court: 14-10-2014
legal_representation: Accused: Rajesh Mahale and Krutin R. Joshi. State of Karnataka: V.N. Raghupathy and Sanjay R. Hegde
investigation_status: Unnatural death case registered; inquest held by Taluka Executive Magistrate; suo motu FIR lodged; post-mortem done; accused arrested; chargesheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted. High Court: State's appeal allowed, accused convicted and sentenced. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld
prosecution_argument: Dowry demanded before marriage and balance demanded after; PWs 1-3, as close relatives, were the most natural witnesses and there was no reason to disbelieve them; accused pledged the ornaments
defence_argument: Kodava community has no dowry custom; PWs 1-3 are interested relatives; independent witnesses not examined; payments were marriage expenses and gifts, not dowry; the ornament recovery was inadequate; no evidence of cruelty soon before death
legal_principle_applied: Dowry death under s.304-B IPC requires death within seven years of marriage by burns or unnatural means, cruelty or harassment soon before death in relation to dowry demand; the resulting presumption against the husband or relative is rebuttable
precedent_relied_upon: Bansi Lal v. State of Haryana (2011) 11 SCC 359; Thanu Ram v. State of M.P. (2010) 10 SCC 353; Rajesh Bhatnagar v. State of Uttarakhand (2012) 7 SCC 91
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (Supreme Court affirmed the High Court's findings and sentence without separate sentencing reasons)
other_sentence_order: High Court directed return of dowry (Rs 15,000 and gold ornaments) or recovery of their value and Rs 15,000 as fine under ss.421-422 Cr.P.C.; left undisturbed by the Supreme Court
